title: The person; the gods enter through the doors of the body (1.2)
hook: the gods are offered a cow, then a horse, as a home, and turn both down. then they see a human being
tomorrow: hunger and thirst ask for a place

segments.voice: Yesterday: atma, the self alone, which looked and said, let me create worlds. Your line was the worlds.

The worlds are made, and the Aitareya has a house-hunting story. The self shapes a cosmic person and draws the great powers out of it: fire, wind, the sun, the moon. Gods. But the gods have nowhere to live. They're adrift, the text says, fallen into a great ocean, and they come back asking for a home. So the self brings them a cow. The gods look it over: no, this isn't enough for us. It brings them a horse. Not enough either. Then it brings them a human being.
screen: `THE GODS HAVE NOWHERE TO LIVE.` → `A COW? NOT ENOUGH.` → `A HORSE? NOT ENOUGH.` → `THEN, A PERSON.`

segments.voice: When the gods see the person, purusha, they say: sukritam bata. Well made, indeed! The person is truly well made, the text adds. That's the Upanishad's verdict on the human body. Not a prison. Not a burden. A good piece of work, the house the gods accepted. Then the self says: enter, each into your own place. And no god just walks in. Each one changes shape to fit. Fire becomes speech, and enters the mouth. Wind becomes breath, and enters the nostrils. The sun becomes sight, and enters the eyes. The directions of space become hearing, and enter the ears. Plants and trees become the hairs, and enter the skin. The moon becomes mind, and enters the heart. Death becomes the down-going breath, and enters the navel. The waters become seed, and enter the organ of generation. Read that list slowly and the body looks different. On this map, when you talk, there's fire in your mouth. When you look up, the sun is looking out through you. Your quiet, changeable mind is the moon. Even death has a room in the house, low down, at the navel, doing its work. The Upanishad isn't asking you to worship your eyes. It's saying the great powers out there and the small doors in here belong to one system, and the person is where they meet. Perhaps that's why a cow wasn't enough, and a horse wasn't enough. They needed a place where speech, sight, mind and the rest could all live together.
screen: `WELL MADE, INDEED!` · `ENTER, EACH INTO YOUR PLACE.` · `FIRE TO SPEECH, SUN TO SIGHT.` · `THE MOON BECOMES MIND, IN THE HEART.` · then, large: `SUKRITAM BATA.`

segments.voice: Bring attention to your closed mouth, where the story puts fire as speech, then to the breath in the nostrils, the wind, and to the eyes, the sun. Move on to the ears and the directions, the skin and the plants and trees, the heart and the moon as mind. Then rest in the whole house at once, every door open.
The person. Purusha, the human being the gods called well made, the one house where fire, wind, sun and moon could each find their door.
Your line: the gods within. Tomorrow, two more guests knock at the door. Four hundred days, done.

howItsDone: In Vedic and later Hindu ritual, the body's senses are linked to deities, and some rites include touching the limbs while reciting mantras, a practice called nyasa, which echoes the idea of the gods dwelling in the body.
